Messages.Author: Talo...@nospam.hotmail.com
Messages.Body:
What is the official word on the following kinds of procedural errors?

1)Player A controlling Egotha(read) untaps and proceeds with his
minion phase. After several actions he realizeds he didnt ask his
prey to burn a card for Egotha's special abilty. His prey complains
it is too late, Player A maintains that it is a required effect.

2)Player B's minion is tapped out and cannot untap to various effects
(mind numb, mind rape, etc) . He untaps his minion and takes actions
with the minion he would not be able to take, the table doesnt notice
until his turn is over.

In both cases the argument could be that A-its too late to go back, or
B-there was a required effect that should have taken place but the
players forgot.

In a disagreement, is there an official rule, VEKN or otherwise, that
covers this?

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
<Talo...@nospam.hotmail.com> wrote in message news:3cd88587.197892006@news...

>
> What is the official word on the following kinds of procedural errors?
>
> 1)Player A controlling Egotha(read) untaps and proceeds with his
> minion phase. After several actions he realizeds he didnt ask his
> prey to burn a card for Egotha's special abilty. His prey complains
> it is too late, Player A maintains that it is a required effect.

Whenever possible the turn should be rewound to the point where the error was
made. The mandatory effect is taken care of and then play proceeds as normal.
Unless something significant has taken place that prevents rewinding, that is
how to proceed.

> 2)Player B's minion is tapped out and cannot untap to various effects
> (mind numb, mind rape, etc) . He untaps his minion and takes actions
> with the minion he would not be able to take, the table doesnt notice
> until his turn is over.

Once the table notices, the first thing to try to do would be to rewind the game
back to the point of the error. If that isn't possible, the judge should impose
some other remedy to square the situation.

> In both cases the argument could be that A-its too late to go back,

> B-there was a required effect that should have taken place but the
> players forgot.
>
> In a disagreement, is there an official rule, VEKN or otherwise, that
> covers this?

If I understand correctly, it is handled the following way:

1. Rewind to point of error (if possible)
2. Skip back to point of error and pop forward if rewinding isn't possible.
3. Judge imposes another remedy to keep things fair.

The way to handle this is officially how to remedy the situation (unless I've
bungled it in which case LSJ will correct this with the real official answer).
Something to this effect should see print in the next update of the tournament
rules.

-Robert

Chairman, V:EKN

> What if someone plays a card, and then someone on the table notices
> that he cannot do this.
> The card has been played, so taking in it back in your hand would be
> against the rules of showing your hand to the other players.

Playing the card is against the rules, so the card has not been played.
Rewind to the point of error (issue warnings or other penalties as
necessary) and continue from that (non-error) point, if possible.

If any significant activity has occurred since the error (e.g., someone
played a Wake to block the action which was illegal), then the judge
should make whatever arrangements are necessary to preserve the
integrity of the game (making sure that no player gets any benefit from
the error, esp. the player committing the error).

> OTOH making the player reshuffle it in his deck can lead to abuse
> (easy cycling when you pretend to play a card you can't.)

This would almost never be appropriate.

> And what happens with the card the player drew when he replaced the
> misplayed card.

Shuffled back into the library (unless some other player had reason to
know the identity of that card, in which case some other appropriate
arrangement should be made by the judge).

As you posted elsewhere in this thread, I would (as a judge)
say that in general you can't "rewind" if anything significant
has happened in the game since the error. As a judge, I
don't want to step in and have players pick up multiple cards,
untap their vampires, etc. It's too messy and unlikely to
produce correct results. ("correct" meaning "what would have
happened if everyone had played correctly in the first place".)

In this case, I'd probably rule that Egothha's prey burns the
top card of her library now (not the same one, right) but
Egothha doesn't gain blood if it's a master card (no one
should benefit from the error). Egothha's controller certainly
gets a warning; if you want to instill the idea that everyone
in a game is responsible for making sure the rules are followed,
everyone at the table could get a warning (or caution).

> >> 2)Player B's minion is tapped out and cannot untap to various effects
> >> (mind numb, mind rape, etc) . He untaps his minion and takes actions
> >> with the minion he would not be able to take, the table doesnt notice
> >> until his turn is over.
>

> Assume this person has taken multiple actions and/or his turn is over.
> I would think it impossible to go back at this point. Would you void
> the effect of the minions action that could not have been taken? Or
> would you allow multiple actions to be 'voided' as the controller
> might have based his choices on the incorrect situation?
>
> Or neither, and let the situation stand?

I would void the effects of the illegally-untapped minion's
action. No cards get picked up etc. The illegal untapper
gets a warning. You might again want to caution all the other
players at the table for not preventing the illegal action
from taking place.

These kinds of decisions are pretty much entirely up to the
judge. You're right that the VEKN tournament rules don't
give a whole lot of guidance as to exactly what is appropriate;
it's basically just judge's discretion as to how to fix things.

It would be nice if there were more examples and suggestions
about what's appropriate in what kinds of situations in the
VEKN tournament rules (guidelines for judges), and I think the
VEKN is planning to put more in when they get a chance.

> >If I understand correctly, it is handled the following way:
> >
> >1. Rewind to point of error (if possible)
> >2. Skip back to point of error and pop forward if rewinding isn't
possible.
> >3. Judge imposes another remedy to keep things fair.

> I assume those are VEKN rules then? And that the judge is the final

> arbiter on wheither rewinds are possible, etc.?
>
> Are partial rewinds allowed?

Anything the judge thinks is appropriate is allowed. :-) In
my judging experience, #2 seems to be the most frequently
appropriate solution, since when a judge is called over it's
rare that nothing has happened and it's possible to rewind
and correct the error (#1).

Josh

the honorable judge roughneck presiding

If Egothha gains a blood, that's good for Egothha's controller.
It's therefore bad for everyone else at the table (not just
prey). We don't know if the error "caused" Egothha to gain
a blood or not because we don't know if Egothha would have
gained a blood if his ability were played correctly.

You're right that I didn't state it properly, though. If
the card that should have been burned and the card that
actually is burned don't match on "is a master card,"
someone has to gain from the error. It's either going to
be "Egothha's controller" or "everyone else depending on
table situation". (In some cases, other players at the
table will also want Egothha to have more blood, but
usually both Egothha's prey and predator won't.) I'd
generally think that it's more important that Egothha's
controller doesn't gain from the error than that others
don't, since it's (first) Egothha's controller's
responsibility to play his ability correctly. But this is
why I might caution/warn *everyone* at the table when this
happens, and not just Egothha's controller. :-)

Josh

>

The difference is, there *is* a correct result for Egothha's
effect. There *was* a correct card to burn and its status
(master card or not) isn't random, it's already known (except
that we don't know which card it was).

Suppose we *do* know which card it was, because we can "count
back" to which card would have been burned at the correct
time. Should we then have Egothha gain blood or not based
on what that card actually is? Or should we just figure that
"the ability is random" and therefore have him gain blood or
not based on the card we actually (incorrectly, to correct for
the error) burn?

> Egothha's controller is not gaining a benefit from the error
> - the error hasn't changed anything there. Similarly, Egothha's
> actual ability.

It's hard to say exactly what is or isn't appropriate. I
guess you're right that prohibiting Egothha from gaining a
blood when later burning a card to correct having missed
the ability is really a "punishment" and not just a
"correction". Still, I might be more comfortable doing it
that way because it *is* a benefit to Egothha's controller
for him to gain a blood, whether random or not.

Josh
